newsitem.title: USA: Magainin trades shrs for royalty interest.
newsitem.headline: Magainin trades shrs for royalty interest.

text.p: Magainin Pharmaceuticals Inc said Thursday it has reached an agreement to buy out a royalty interest it would have owed on any sales of MSI-78, which is being studied for use in treating infections in diabetic foot ulcers, resulting in an expected charge of $7.1 million.

Under the deal, Magainin will issue 550,000 shares of its common stock to Houghten Pharmaceuticals Inc and Scripps Research Institute. In exchange, it retains a full royalty interest in MSI-78, the companies said in separate statements.
In connection with the transaction, Magainin said it expects to record a non-cash charge of about $7.1 million, which it said is the value of the issued shares.

"Assuming MSI-78 is successfully developed and commercialized, this buyout will result in greater cash flows to Magainin, and improved margins on sales of MSI-78," Magainin Chairman, President and Chief Executive Jay Moorin said in a statement.
Under the original agreement, a Houghten subsidiary, Multiple Peptide Systems Inc, and the institute were to license the compounds in exchange for royalties on sales.
Houghten said it will split the 550,000 shares equally with the Scripps Institute. The company said the royalty arrangement for other compounds covered in the original agreement will remain intact.

On Wednesday, Magainin reported successful results of its initial Phase III clinical trial of MSI-78 for treatment of infection in diabetic foot ulcers. Results from a second such trial are expected to be available in the first quarter of 1997.
